$comment: Conformance corpus for the RegistryKey grammar (registry-kernel ticket 05). Data, not PHP, so the TS port (ticket 16) and the enum codegen (ticket 12) assert against the SAME cases rather than a re-reading of the prose. Every entry here is executable: tests/Unit/Registries/KeyTest.php drives all three sections. Longest-prefix ROUTING cases are deliberately absent — the index does not exist yet; ticket 21 adds a fourth section when it lands.

grammar.why: single segment is a legal key
kebab inside a segment; the estate's resource-key convention is plural-kebab
a live resource key, post api-surface-coherence ticket 16
a live invocable name in this package's own tests
digits are legal within a segment
empty string is not a key
uppercase is REJECTED, never folded — the whole case-sensitivity decision in one line
camelCase is a class name, not a key; use Key::fromClass() deliberately
`:` means artisan command namespacing (splicewire:beam:doctor) and type-tagged identity (fact:secret) live in this estate — it is not an alternate dot
`/` means a composer coordinate, and a MIME type; not a key separator
empty segment
leading separator
trailing separator
no trimming — whitespace in a source literal is a typo and must fail loudly
same, trailing
the `$`-vs-`\z` regex trap: a trailing newline prints identically to a legal key
snake — api-surface-coherence ticket 16 spent real effort removing snake keys from the estate
leading hyphen
trailing hyphen
doubled hyphen

REGRESSION PIN: unreachable under the charset, and that is the point — this case fails loudly the day anyone adds case folding to either runtime. PHP strtolower() and JS toLowerCase() disagree on the Turkish dotted I.
non-ASCII is out, so the two runtimes have no locale to disagree about

equality.why: one character of difference in the last segment is a different key
NOT the same key — though EnumWriter::caseName() currently emits BeamRealmOverlays for both, which is ticket 12's collision to solve, not the grammar's

hierarchy.why: strictly below; a key is not under itself
THE case this exists for: prefix is segment-wise, never character-wise
